$comment: Audit item #160. A fixture is a claim about what upstream sends. Nothing
recorded where these came from, when, or what they are supposed to prove,
so a fixture that had drifted away from reality looked exactly like one
that had not -- and a test passing against a stale fixture is worse than
no test, because it reports confidence it has not earned.
'digest' is over the canonical JSON (sorted keys, compact separators), not
the file bytes. Line endings differ between a Windows working tree and a
Linux runner, and a formatter may reflow the file; neither changes what the
fixture asserts. A byte hash would fail for both and teach people to
'staleness' is either 'pinned' -- a deliberate point-in-time capture, with
the reason -- or a 'revalidate_by' date. Editing a fixture changes its
digest, which fails until this file is updated, which is the point: the
provenance cannot drift away from the data without someone noticing.

proves: The scoring table, squad rules and chip definitions the engine reads.
Trimmed to the fields rules.py validates; the live payload is 1.3 MB.
pinned_because: These are the 2026-27 rules as published before the season. The value
of the fixture is that it does not move: a test asserting the engine
scores a hat-trick correctly must keep asserting it against the rules
that were in force, not against whatever is served today.
Drift against the live endpoint is caught by the Live FPL Contracts
workflow, which runs daily against the real bootstrap and fails when
a controlling rule appears, disappears or changes shape. That is a
better staleness check than a date, because it asks upstream rather

proves: An entry before a ball is kicked: current_event is null and there is
no picks endpoint yet. The engine must answer 'no processed event'
rather than treating the manager as having an empty squad.
Identifying fields are replaced; no real manager is described.
pinned_because: The pre-season state exists for about three weeks a year and cannot
be recaptured outside that window. Losing this fixture would mean
losing the only test of the state the site opens in.

proves: The shape of a StatsBomb lineups document: two teams, each with a
lineup of players carrying positions and substitution windows.
Player and club names are invented.
pinned_because: Constructed rather than captured, so there is nothing upstream to be
stale against. It describes a format, and the format is versioned by
StatsBomb rather than dated. If schema_version here stops matching
what the adapter expects, that is the signal, not the age.
